name: John Wayne Orange County International Airport
before:
The airport for Orange County, and the second busiest in the Greater Los Angeles area with more than 10 million passengers in 2024. For a client heading to Newport Beach, Irvine or Costa Mesa it is far more convenient than the alternatives.

The runway is the thing to understand. At 5,700 feet the main runway is the shortest in the United States handling regularly scheduled international flights, and no scheduled passenger aircraft larger than a 757 has ever operated here. No widebody has ever flown a scheduled service in. That shapes which carriers and which routes are possible.

There are 22 gates in total. Southwest, American, United, Delta and Alaska are the main airlines. General aviation movements actually outnumber commercial ones.

The code SNA comes from Santa Ana, which sits just across Interstate 405. The airport was renamed in 1979 after John Wayne, who lived nearby in Newport Beach and died that year, and a statue of him was put up in the terminal in 1982.
after:
The airport for Orange County, and the second busiest in the Greater Los Angeles area, with more than 11.3 million passengers in 2025. For a client heading to Newport Beach or elsewhere in Orange County it is far more convenient than the alternatives.

The runway is the thing to understand. At 5,700 feet the main runway is short, and that shapes which carriers and routes are possible. Scheduled flights go across the US and to Mexico and Canada.

The airport counts 20 commercial passenger gates plus two small commuter terminals. Southwest, American, United, Alaska and Delta are the main airlines. General aviation movements outnumber commercial ones.

Its code, SNA, comes from Santa Ana. The airport was renamed in 1979 after the late John Wayne, who lived nearby in Newport Beach. A bronze statue of him, dedicated in 1982, stands on the arrivals level between the A and B baggage claims.

claims.claim: more than 11.3 million passengers in 2025

claims.note: Was 'more than 10 million passengers in 2024' (the operator gives 11,089,405 for 2024). TOTAL passengers, arriving plus departing: 11,369,865 in 2025, up 2.5 per cent (operator's December 2025 release). The FAA's preliminary table counts 5,521,729 boardings (about half of total passengers), consistent with it, and the City of Newport Beach gives about 11.3 million a year. The operator's own overview page says 'approximately 11.7 million annual passengers', which is not tied to a year and is not used.

claims.claim: curfew and access limits
claims.why: Held back: a warning that replaces nothing in the old text. For Andy: the operator says airline operations are regulated by an Access Plan that 'places restrictions on operational capacity, hours of operations, and noise levels' under the 1985 Settlement Agreement, which the City of Newport Beach also describes; Wikipedia gives the curfew as no commercial departures from 10 pm to 7 am (8 am on Sundays) and no commercial arrivals from 11 pm to 7 am. The curfew hours themselves would need the operator's own curfew page before being added.

sources.org: John Wayne Airport (County of Orange, operator, ocair.com)
sources.quote: Commercial Air Carrier operations at JWA are regulated by the Access Plan, which places restrictions on operational capacity, hours of operations, and noise levels

In 1985, the City, the County of Orange, the Airport Working Group (AWG), and Stop Polluting Our Newport (SPON) entered into a Settlement Agreement to resolve litigation related to John Wayne Airport (JWA).
The county prohibits commercial departures between 10:00 PM and 7:00 AM (8:00 AM on Sundays) and commercial arrivals between 11:00 PM and 7:00 AM (8:00 AM on Sundays).

opinion.why: The old text's framing, kept in softer form. Wikipedia calls it the shortest US runway with regularly scheduled international flights and says passenger jets here have never been larger than a 757; those details rest on Wikipedia alone, so the text says only that the runway is short.
